title: Continually Evolving Skill Knowledge in Vision Language Action Model
claim: A continual-learning system that retains and evolves knowledge across tasks outperforms leading baselines on every simulated and real-world benchmark.
layout: Left robot-state progression, central knowledge hub, four bar-chart bubbles fanning right
description: A busy composite figure. On the left, stacked photos of a dual-arm humanoid robot show a progression from a confused or overwhelmed 'Common VLA' (thinking and shocked emojis, faded images) to a confident 'Stellar VLA' (smiling, flexing-arm emoji). Colored lines in blue, green and yellow run from task photos at the top down into a glowing central blob labeled 'Knowledge Evolution'. Linked colored nodes sit on the blob, and the large 'Stellar VLA' logo with a star icon sits beneath it. From the blob, translucent colored cones fan out to four rounded bubbles on the right. Each bubble holds a small bar chart comparing UniVLA, π0.5, T-Stellar and TS-Stellar on LIBERO-goal, LIBERO-long, LIBERO-30* and Real-world. The Stellar bars are highlighted and tallest. caption: Illustration of {Stellar VLA}. T-Stellar and TS-Stellar outperform UniVLA [ref] and $\pi_{0.5}$ [ref] in final average success rates across simulation and real-world dual-arm experiments.
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models show promising knowledge accumulation ability through pretraining, yet continual learning remains challenging. Existing continual imitation learning (CIL) methods often require additional parameters or modules, limiting scalability for large VLA models. We propose Stellar VLA, a knowledge-driven CIL framework without parameter growth, featuring two variants: T-Stellar for task-centric modeling and TS-Stellar for hierarchical modeling of reusable skills across tasks. Stellar VLA jointly optimizes task representations and a self-evolving knowledge space, with knowledge-posterior-guided expert routing using knowledge relations and Top-K semantic embeddings for task specialization. Experiments on LIBERO demonstrate strong performance against VLA and CIL baselines with only 1% replay. Dual-arm real-world experiments validate knowledge transfer across embodiments and scenes. TS-Stellar excels in hierarchical manipulation, while visualizations demonstrate knowledge retention and task discovery. Project Website: https://stellarvla.github.io/
